# FerroFED's self-assessment against the MyHealth@EU Requirements Catalogue
# v10.0.0 (W10-Operation Ready, 2026-03-06): one row for every requirement
# id of the catalogue, and one for its exception handling (1.25), with the
# gateway's status and the page or test that shows it. It is
# FerroFED's own reading, not a MyHealth@EU compliance check, and confers no
# Operation Ready status. The book page website/book/src/evaluate/myhealth-eu.md
# and the README badge are rendered from it by scripts/conformance/myhealth-eu.sh.
# The catalogue is privileged-access (Xt-EHR D6.1 section 5; Commission
# Decision 2011/833/EU Art 2(2)(c)) and FerroFED has no grant to reuse it, so
# this file holds requirement ids, section numbers, statuses and FerroFED's
# own conclusions, and never a word of catalogue text.
# Columns: id (the catalogue's requirement id); section (its section number
# in the catalogue); status (met, partly-met, waits-art-15-1, not-met,
# not-assessed or not-applicable), which judges the gateway's share of the
# requirement and counts every row but not-applicable as binding the
# gateway; evidence (one or more items separated by "; ", each a file of
# this repository, optionally followed by "::" and a heading of a Markdown
# file or the name of a test function of a Rust file); issue (#N, several
# separated by one space, or -);
# note (FerroFED's conclusion in its own words: what the gateway does and
# whose the rest is).
# scripts/checks/myhealth-eu.sh holds every row to the id list, the tree,
# the rendered page and badge, and the no-catalogue-text rule. No
# specification governs the form: our own design.

column6: The gateway lists every prescription each member makes available, its own FHIR ones and those mapped from its openEHR medication orders, each with its patient, prescriber and Provenance; which prescriptions are available abroad is each member's selection.

A member's prescription passes through unchanged, so its content and missing-data reasons are the member's; a mapped prescription carries what the medication order records in the HL7 Europe MPD profiles, and the gateway writes no missing-data reason for a basic element the order lacks.

The gateway writes a dispensation to the member that owns the prescription and answers with its creation or relays its refusal; substitution belongs to the country of treatment and the owner.
The gateway checks a dispensation against its profile and requires its identifier, which the owner stores; its content is the country of treatment's.
Transcoding the dispensation is the contact points' (2026/2083 Art 3(4)), and its exchange runs over their secure network (Art 3(6)).
The gateway confirms only after the owner created the dispensation and never sends it twice; updating the available prescriptions is the owner's.

The face takes a discard as an update with status entered-in-error by its own id, held to its profile and written once to the member that holds the dispensation; one sent again as a new dispensation is refused as a duplicate.

As national infrastructure behind the access service, the gateway serves a person's own grant every category the face serves, confined to them: their summary, laboratory, discharge and imaging reports, and prescriptions where members serve them, each downloadable in its exchange format.
Translating a document for patient access is the central terminology service the contact point asks (2026/2083 Art 3(1)(b) and (4)); the gateway translates no document.
The list of languages comes from the central terminology service the contact point asks (2026/2083 Art 3(1)(b) and (4)); the gateway holds no translations.
The gateway serves a person's own grant their data of every category it serves and records each access with the person as caller and subject; display is the access service's.
The gateway exchanges sectioned, coded data with codes as recorded, an equivalent coding only for an exact mapping, and a narrative in the original language.
